title: SBA 504 loans
metaDescription: SBA 504 loans provide long-term, fixed-asset financing for owner-occupied commercial real estate and major equipment. Learn when the program commonly fits and how it differs from 7(a).
summary: The SBA 504 page covers fixed-asset SBA financing used for owner-occupied property and major equipment projects.

hero.title: SBA 504 loans — for real estate and major assets.
hero.lead: The SBA 504 program is designed for long-term investments in fixed assets like owner-occupied property and heavy equipment. Use this page to understand when it commonly fits and how it differs from other paths.

quickAnswer.definition: is a long-term, fixed-asset financing program from the U.S. Small Business Administration, delivered through Certified Development Companies and lenders. It is typically used to buy, build, or improve owner-occupied commercial real estate or to purchase major equipment.

whoItFits.heading: When SBA 504 tends to fit
items: Constructing or renovating an existing facility
Buying long-life, heavy equipment or machinery

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When SBA 504 may not fit as well
items: Working capital and inventory needs generally point to other structures.
Borrowers without a qualifying owner-occupied asset project may find a different product is more flexible.

eligibilityCards.title: Owner-occupied use
eligibilityCards.description: The 504 program generally requires the business to occupy a qualifying share of the property.

eligibilityCards.title: Eligible fixed assets
eligibilityCards.description: Proceeds are directed to qualifying long-term assets such as real estate and heavy equipment.

eligibilityCards.title: Repayment strength
eligibilityCards.description: Lenders assess business cash flow and project viability during underwriting.

sectionDisclosureHtml: Fund44 is not a lender, a CDC, or the SBA. SBA 504 eligibility, occupancy rules, and terms are set by SBA program rules, CDCs, and approved lenders — not by Fund44. This page is educational only.

commonQuestions.question: What is the SBA 504 loan used for?
commonQuestions.answer: SBA 504 financing is generally used for owner-occupied commercial real estate, construction or renovation, and major long-life equipment. It is not typically used for working capital or inventory.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between SBA 504 and 7(a)?
commonQuestions.answer: SBA 504 is focused on long-term fixed assets like real estate and heavy equipment, while SBA 7(a) is more flexible and can cover working capital, acquisition, and more. See our SBA 7(a) vs 504 guide in the learning hub.

commonQuestions.question: Does 504 require owner occupancy?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes — the 504 program includes owner-occupancy requirements for real estate. The exact thresholds are defined by SBA program rules and your lender or CDC.

commonQuestions.question: Does Fund44 issue SBA 504 loans?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Fund44 does not issue SBA 504 loans. Eligibility and terms are decided by lenders, CDCs, and SBA program rules.
